topic: Discovery stories / peptides your body makes: somatostatin, the body's 'off switch' peptide, and the first working peptide made by bacteria from a lab-built gene. 1973: Brazeau, Guillemin et al. isolate a 14-amino-acid peptide from sheep hypothalamus that inhibits growth hormone release (Science 1973); made in brain, gut and pancreas, inhibits gut, pancreas and pituitary secretions, half-life 1-3 min (StatPearls 2023); 1977: Itakura, Boyer et al. chemically synthesize the somatostatin gene, express it in E. coli, the first functional polypeptide from a chemically synthesized gene (Science 1977)
style: Lab notebook: off-white graph paper with blue 5 mm grid and red margin line, Caveat 700 handwritten headlines in blue-black ink, Atkinson Hyperlegible body, yellow and pink highlighter swipes, date stamps like notebook entries, hand-drawn underline

Lab note · 1977

Bacteria were taught to make a hormone.

Its job: saying STOP.

Lab note · 1973

A brake in the brain.

Found in sheep brains by Roger Guillemin's team.

It blocked growth hormone release.

14

amino acids

Somatostatin.

Made in your brain, gut and pancreas.

The body's off switch.

  • Slows pituitary signals
  • Slows pancreas signals
  • Slows gut signals

Gone in 1–3 minutes.

Lab note · 1977

Scientists built its gene with chemistry.

E. coli bacteria then made the hormone.

A world first for a lab‑built gene.

Save this for your biochem exam.
